built.saved_results: src/vacancy_derived.py: per-version results in table vacancy_derived, invalidated automatically when rule source files change, prepared in the background at service start and every 30 s.
built.list_queries: src/archive_store.py filters and sorts on saved facts and reads payloads only for returned rows. Index membership_entity added.
built.payload_callers: Calls with include_payload read the real text and bypass saved facts, because they select jobs to act on.
built.opportunities_api: GET /archive/analytics accepts history=false and evidence=false. New: /archive/analytics/status, /history, /evidence.
built.ui: archive-web/busy.js spinner with real progress bar. The opportunities screen draws in stages, loads history and evidence separately, and batches large maps. The vacancy list, detail and map show spinners.

equivalence_check.method: HEAD code and new code run on separate copies of the same archive.
equivalence_check.excluded: Row order of unranked lists (changed on purpose in stage 1) and last_seen.

limits: Timings are from one Mac, using temporary copies of the archive, in headless Chrome.

The first run after install, or after editing a rule file, takes about a minute for the opportunities screen and shows real progress. The trajectory filter can then take about 40 s, with a spinner, until preparation finishes.
Text search still scans descriptions; fast here at 0.18 s, but it will grow with the archive.
No long tasks were recorded, but this is headless Chrome, so it does not prove smoothness on a busy desktop.
Not yet run against the real archive. It prepares itself the next time the service starts.

follow_ups.favicon_401: The unexplained 401 console errors were /favicon.ico, which required auth. Fixed with an inline icon in index.html.
follow_ups.login_form: The token input now sits in a form, which removes the Chrome password-field warning and lets Enter submit.
follow_ups.domexception_message: On the user's first real run the screen showed 'Cannot set property message ...'. api() and showDiagnostic assigned to the read-only DOMException.message, hiding the real error. Fixed, with a regression test.
follow_ups.original_error_unknown: The underlying error was not identified. The bug hid it. A cold-cache run on an archive copy (8000 vacancies, no background jobs) showed no failed requests and the list appeared within 90 s. Likely but unproven: a request timing out during first preparation on the real service, or a non-timeout DOMException. If it recurs, the message now names the endpoint.
